text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Arab states threaten to freeze ties.

- August CPI up 0.4 percent, housing down 0.8 percent. Manufacturers Association President Dan Propper says relatively low increase due to shekel's performance against foreign currencies rather than government monetary policy.
- Syria transfers more than 10,000 soldiers from the Beirut area to the Bekaa Valley in Lebanon.
- Chances lessen for holding a regional economic conference in Cairo in November.
- U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk says President Bill Clinton wanted to free spy Jonathan Pollard but security establishment opposed it.
- The reason for the low CPI -- the drop in the dollar exchange rate which lowered the price of housing.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: I'll not agree to give up on sacred assets for the benefit of relations with the United States.
- Arab foreign ministers: Without peace progress -- we'll freeze relations with Israel.
- Netanyahu says Israel keeping a close eye on Syrian troop movements. Fear of limited Syrian action in Hermon area.
- Message from Syria to Israel via the United States: We've no intention of attacking. Assessment is troops are deployed for defensive purposes. But situation could get out of control.
- Fear of tourism crisis: Hotels in Eilat are half-full on Rosh Hashana, the Jewish new year.
